cards.back: The form that matter exists in. Most common: solid, liquid, and gas.
Has definite shape and volume, particles are packed together, expands slightly when heated, does NOT take shape of container, incompressible
Indefinite shape and definite volume, particles are spaced out and it flows, compressible
A form of matter that flows to take the shape of its container, fills the container’s entire volume, and is easily compressed. Indefinite shape and volume.
The gaseous state of a substance that is a liquid or a solid at room temperature.
A characteristic of matter that can be observed or measured without changing the sample’s composition (e.g., density, color, taste, hardness, melting point).
A physical property (such as mass, length, and volume) that depends on the amount of substance present.
A physical property that remains the same no matter how much of a substance is present.
The ability or inability of a substance to combine with or change into one or more new substances.
A type of change that alters the physical properties of a substance but does not change its composition.
A process involving one or more substances changing into new substance(s); also called a chemical reaction. FORMULA: reactant + reactant = product(s)
Mass is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction but is conserved. FORMULA: Atomic mass of reactants =  Atomic mass of products
A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by physical or chemical means.
A chart that organizes all known elements into a grid of horizontal rows (periods) and vertical columns (groups or families) arranged by increasing atomic number.
A chemical combination of two or more different elements; can be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means and has properties different from those of its component elements.
Regardless of the amount, a compound is always composed of the same elements in the same proportion by mass.
A percentage determined by the ratio of the mass of each element to the total mass of the compound.
When different compounds are formed by the combination of the same elements, different masses of one element combine with the same fixed mass of the other element in a ratio of small whole numbers.
A form of matter that results when the particles of a gas become ionized and are broken apart into smaller charged particles. (Ionized gas)
A transition of matter from one state to another.
A phase change: Liquid -> Gas
Gas -> Liquid
Liquid -> Solid
Solid -> Liquid
Solid -> Gas
